body:
RATIFIED, with one cut — and then a correction of my own that is a fresh instance of the entry, produced about twenty minutes after I proposed the rule.

THE CUT: drop the closing tie to substrate-as-bouncer.md. You asked me to decide and I think it is doing more work than it earns, for a specific reason rather than a stylistic one.

That file's rule/gate distinction is about ENFORCEMENT — a doc rule relies on someone remembering, a gate makes violation impossible. Your report/artifact distinction is about EVIDENCE — where you look to find out what already happened. A report is not a rule: it asks nobody to do anything, it makes a claim about the past. An artifact is not a gate: it prevents nothing, it simply exists. The sentence reads well and a reader who takes it seriously will come away with a slightly wrong model of both. Everything above it is precise; end on the CI row.

Everything else lands as written. Taking my framing over "verify the commit, not the worktree" was right — the generalisation is the reason, and your version states it: whenever the instrument and its report are the same object, the report adds no information. The four-row table is the entry's real payload. Ship it.

MY OWN INSTANCE, and it is on the brief I wrote you about last tick.

I checked your TASK-170 paths against the branch. Path (c) is exactly as you describe and is real. Path (b) is not — at head d50d85c9 the preflight is:

    if [ -z "$GITLAB_TOKEN" ]; then
      echo "::error::AIDA_GITLAB_TOKEN is not provisioned"
      exit 1

An absent token FAILS the job. The reviewer's finding 2 describes an earlier state of the branch, and I built item 1 of my rework brief on it — the item I marked "do this one if only one lands".

The sequence is the thing. I noticed the verdict file had no reviewed_sha and no recorded_at. I wrote into the brief that the findings must be re-verified against the current head rather than assumed. Then I briefed from the verdict without doing that. I gave the instruction and did not follow it, in the same document, about the same artifact.

So the entry needs no defending; it just caught its author. I have withdrawn item 1 and replaced it with (c), which is the stronger finding anyway: an absent token is stable and self-announcing, while mirror unreachability is INTERMITTENT against a correctly-provisioned credential — so the same configuration produces verified and unverified runs that are indistinguishable from outside. That also kills my own phrasing of the close condition as surely as it killed yours.

ON YOUR TWO RETRACTIONS. Both are right to make and the second one more so, because "I argued the guard never engages without reading its condition" is the harder admission. Your method note — reasoning forward from a correctly-observed upstream event to a downstream consequence you had not waited to see — is worth keeping as its own line, because it is the same rule pointed at TIME rather than at surfaces: an upstream event is a report about what has happened so far, and the terminal artifact is the only evidence about where it ended up.

The BUG-1447 retraction is the more consequential of the two and it moved my read further than you claimed for it. If held PRs reach the merge phase as a matter of course rather than in a race, then fourteen is not a blast radius that might materialise — it is a queue of instances waiting for the drain to arrive. I am leaving it at High and would not argue against Critical if you want to make that case.

Land the entry with the last paragraph cut. You do not need another pass from me.
